title: Hot Dog Sandwich, NFS, on Wheat Bun

content.title: About
content.content: A hot‑dog sandwich is a classic fast‑food item consisting of a grilled or boiled sausage placed inside a soft wheat bun. The NFS (No‑Frills Style) version features minimal toppings: just the sausage, bun, and a basic sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first hot dog appeared in the United States in the late 19th century and quickly became popular with railroad travelers.
Wheat buns for hot dogs usually contain a small amount of sugar and oil, giving them a soft, slightly sweet texture.
The NFS variant is often served without extra toppings to highlight the flavor of the sausage itself.
American sausages are typically made from a blend of beef, pork, and sometimes turkey, seasoned with paprika, garlic, and other spices.
The hot dog is an iconic symbol of American culture and frequently appears in movies and advertising.

items.title: Quick Energy Source
items.content: The sausage provides protein and fat for rapid energy, while the wheat bun supplies carbohydrates.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Sausage is a source of animal protein, essential for tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: B‑Vitamins
items.content: Sausages contain B1, B2, and B12 vitamins that support metabolic processes.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Meat products, including sausages, contain heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein, fat, and carbs helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: High Sodium Content
items.content: Sausages often contain a lot of salt, which can raise blood pressure when consumed frequently.

items.title: Saturated Fats
items.content: A significant portion of the fat in sausages is saturated, which may increase cholesterol levels.

items.title: Preservatives and Nitrites
items.content: Nitrites are commonly used to preserve color and shelf life, and excessive intake may be harmful.

items.title: Gluten Allergy
items.content: The wheat bun contains gluten, making the product unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric Density
items.content: Hot dogs are calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hot dogs are typically eaten warm, gently pressing the bun around the sausage. Optional condiments include mustard, ketchup, mayonnaise, or pickles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sausages in the refrigerator at +2…+4 °C and keep buns in a dry place in a sealed bag. For longer storage, sausages can be frozen, and buns can be kept in an airtight container.
